question_text: A light source emitting a light of frequency $6 \times 10^{15}\text{ Hz}$ is moving away from an observer with a speed of $4\text{ m/s}$. The apparent change in the frequency of light as observed by the observer will be:
solution:
The apparent change in frequency due to the Doppler effect for light (for $v \ll c$) is given by $\Delta 
u =  rac{v}{c}
u$.
Substituting the values:
$$\Delta 
u =  rac{4	ext{ m/s}}{3 	imes 10^8	ext{ m/s}} 	imes (6 	imes 10^{15}	ext{ Hz}) = 8 	imes 10^7	ext{ Hz}$$

question_text: If two waves $y_1 = \sqrt{3}\sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ and $y_2 = 3\cos\omega t$ interfere at a point, then the amplitude of the resulting wave will be:
solution:
Expressing both waves in sine form:
$$y_1 = \sqrt{3}\sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right), \quad y_2 = 3\sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$$
The phase difference is $\phi = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{6} = 30^\circ$.
The resultant amplitude is:
$$A = \sqrt{A_1^2 + A_2^2 + 2A_1A_2\cos\phi} = \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 + 3^2 + 2(\sqrt{3})(3)\cos 30^\circ} = \sqrt{3 + 9 + 6\sqrt{3}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{21} \approx 4.58 \approx 4.6$$

question_text: A single slit of width $12 \times 10^{-5}\text{ cm}$ is illuminated with light of wavelength $6000\text{ \AA}$. The angular width of the central maximum is:
solution:
The angular width of the central maximum in single-slit diffraction is given by:
$$2\theta = \frac{2\lambda}{a}$$
Given $a = 12 \times 10^{-5}\text{ cm} = 1.2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$ and $\lambda = 6000\text{ \AA} = 6 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$:
$$2\theta = \frac{2 \times 6 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}}{1.2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}} = 1\text{ rad}$$

question_text: Which of the following optical devices produces coherent sources?
solution: Fresnel's biprism divides a single wavefront into two virtual coherent sources by refraction, producing sustained interference patterns.

question_text: For what approximate distance is ray optics a good approximation, when the aperture is $4\text{ mm}$ wide and the wavelength of the light used is $400\text{ nm}$?
solution:
Ray optics remains a good approximation up to the Fresnel distance ($Z_F$):
$$Z_F = \frac{a^2}{\lambda} = \frac{(4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m})^2}{400 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}} = \frac{16 \times 10^{-6}}{4 \times 10^{-7}} = 40\text{ m}$$

question_text: When a film of transparent material of thickness $2.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ cm}$ is placed over one of the slits in YDSE, the fringe pattern shifts by a distance equal to $20$ fringe widths. The refractive index ($\mu$) of the material of the film is (take $\lambda = 5000\text{ \AA}$):
solution:
The fringe shift is given by $\Delta y = \frac{D}{d}(\mu - 1)t = n\beta$, where $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$.
Thus, $(\mu - 1)t = n\lambda$:
$$(\mu - 1) = \frac{n\lambda}{t} = \frac{20 \times (5000 \times 10^{-8}\text{ cm})}{2.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ cm}} = \frac{10^{-3}}{2.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 0.40$$
$$\mu = 1 + 0.40 = 1.40$$

question_text: In YDSE with light of wavelength $\lambda = 5000\text{ \AA}$, the distance between the slits is $0.2\text{ mm}$ and the distance between the plane of slits and screen is $2\text{ m}$. The central maximum is at $y = 0$. The fourth maximum will appear at $y$ equal to:
solution:
The position of the $n^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe is given by:
$$y_n = \frac{n\lambda D}{d}$$
For $n = 4$:
$$y_4 = \frac{4 \times (5000 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}) \times 2\text{ m}}{0.2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}} = \frac{4 \times 10^{-6}}{2 \times 10^{-4}} = 2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m} = 2\text{ cm}$$
